# Estimating the Distribution of Overreporting {#sec-app-deconvolution}

This appendix describes the estimator behind @sec-deconvolution: a spline model of the density of overreporting, fitted to the observed residuals by penalized maximum likelihood, with the distribution of measurement error taken from corporations.

Following @Kang2021, the density of overreporting is a logspline,

$$
f_{u|\Theta}(u)=\exp(s(u;\theta)-C(\theta)), \quad L < u < R,
$$

where $[L,R]$ is the support of $f_u$,

$$
s(u;\theta)=\sum_{j=1}^{K-1}\theta_j B_j(u),
$$

$\{B_j(u), j=1,2,\dots, K\}$ is a sequence of cubic B-spline basis functions, and

$$
C(\theta) = \log\left(\int^R_L \exp(s(u;\theta)) \text{d}u \right) < \infty .
$$

Then $f_{u|\Theta}(u)$ is a positive density on $(L,R)$, twice continuously differentiable. The last basis function is left out for identification: B-splines sum to one, $\sum_{j=1}^{K}B_j(u)=1$ for all $u \in (L,R)$.

Because $\mathcal V_{it}=u_{it}-\varepsilon_{it}$, the log likelihood of the observed residuals is

$$
\begin{aligned}
    l_{\mathcal{V}}(\mathbf{\theta})=&\sum_{i=1}^{n}\log \left(\int f_{\varepsilon}(u-\mathcal{V_i})f_{u|\theta}(u)\text{d}u\right)\\
    =&\sum_{i=1}^{n}\log \left(\int f_{\varepsilon}(u-\mathcal{V_i})\exp(s(u;\theta))\text{d}u\right)-nC(\theta).
\end{aligned}
$$

To avoid overfitting, I subtract a roughness penalty from the log likelihood [@Eilers1996]:

$$
\text{Penalty}(\theta) = \lambda \cdot \|\mathbf{D}\theta \|^2,
$$

where $\mathbf D$ takes third-order differences of adjacent coefficients. Each coefficient weights a B-spline that overlaps only its neighbours: large differences between adjacent coefficients make the log-density $s(u;\theta)$ wiggle, and the penalty keeps it smooth. The estimate $\hat\theta$ maximizes $l_{\mathcal V}(\theta)-\text{Penalty}(\theta)$.

I estimate each industry separately. The density of measurement error, $f_\varepsilon$, is a kernel density of the corporations' residuals, with the Sheather–Jones plug-in bandwidth and exponential tails beyond the range of the data. The support of $u$ is $[0,\max\mathcal V+0.1]$, which imposes $u\ge0$. The spline has eight interior knots at equally spaced percentiles of the non-negative values of $\mathcal V$, and the penalty weight is $\lambda=10$. Adaptive 15-node Gauss–Legendre quadrature computes the integrals in the likelihood, and BFGS maximizes the penalized likelihood. The estimator does not impose that the mean of $u$ equal the mean of $\mathcal V$; the two differ in Printing and publishing (342) and Non-metallic minerals (369).

The sample is the stage-2 sample of @sec-counterfactual: unincorporated firms that pay sales tax on purchases, with a log materials share net of sales taxes above 5 percent (and below 75 percent in Non-metallic minerals, 369), and with the top 0.5 percent by reported materials trimmed. $\mathcal V$ and $f_\varepsilon$ come from the first stage on the net share, with juridical organization codes 6 to 9 excluded. @sec-deconvolution reports the five largest industries where the test rejects at the 1 percent level and the variance condition holds; @sec-app-pf-all reports all nine stage-2 industries.
